question: Which city was chosen to host a major five-day Sumo wrestling tournament in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**London, UK**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The city of **London**, **United Kingdom**, has been officially chosen to host a major five-day **Sumo** wrestling tournament in **October 2025**.
 
• This landmark event, titled "**Grand Sumo London**," is scheduled to take place at the **O2 Arena**, one of the world's most popular music and entertainment venues.
 
• The tournament marks the first time in over **30 years** that the **Japan Sumo Association** has brought a full-scale professional sumo event to **London**; the last occurrence was in **1991** at the **Royal Albert Hall**.
 
• The **five-day** event in **2025** will feature approximately **70 professional rikishi** (wrestlers) traveling from **Japan** to compete.
 
• The roster of participants is expected to include the sport's highest-ranking athletes, including the **Yokozuna** (grand champion) and **Ozeki** (champion), providing a rare opportunity for international fans to witness the elite level of the sport. ***Hence, the correct answer is London, UK.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Sumo Ranking:**
 
 
• The **Banzuke** is the official hierarchy of sumo wrestlers. The top division is known as **Makuuchi**, which contains a fixed number of **42 wrestlers**.
 
• The **Yokozuna** is the pinnacle of the sport; unlike other ranks, a **Yokozuna** cannot be demoted for a poor performance but is expected to retire if they can no longer compete at the highest level.
 
• Other high ranks include **Ozeki**, **Sekiwake**, and **Komusubi**, collectively referred to as the **Sanyaku**.
 
 
 
• **The Playing Area (Dohyo):**
 
 
• Sumo matches take place in a **Dohyo**, a circular ring made of specialized **clay** and covered with a thin layer of sand.
 
• The ring is exactly **4.55 meters** in diameter and is defined by **tawara** (rice-straw bales) buried in the clay.
 
• A wrestler loses the match if any part of his body other than the soles of his feet touches the ground, or if he is pushed outside the circle of the **tawara**.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Types:**
 
 
• Official tournaments, called **Honbasho**, occur **six times a year** in **Japan** (three in **Tokyo**, and one each in **Osaka**, **Nagoya**, and **Fukuoka**).
 
• The **London 2025** event is classified as a **Jungyo** (exhibition tour), which aims to promote the sport and engage with fans outside the standard competitive season.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** The **1991** tournament in **London** was a pivotal moment for the sport's global visibility, marking the first time a **sumo tournament** was held outside **Japan** in its **1,500-year history**.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Sumo is deeply rooted in **Shinto** traditions. Rituals such as **Shiko** (leg stomping to drive away evil spirits) and the throwing of **salt** (to purify the ring) are integral parts of the pre-match ceremony.
 
• **Match Duration:** While the rituals and preparation can take several minutes, the actual bout typically lasts only **10 to 60 seconds**, emphasizing explosive power and technique.
 
• **Governing Body:** All professional sumo is overseen by the **Japan Sumo Association (Nihon Sumo Kyokai)**, based in **Ryogoku**, **Tokyo**.
